Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the recap and the files — I skimmed the draft. A few clarifying questions before we move to a demo:

1) When you say "avoid storing PII," do you mean we can configure Redwood to drop sensitive fields from both request and response logs at ingestion time? Is that deterministic (i.e., deterministic hashing vs one-way redaction)?
2) For trace IDs: we need the ability to correlate traces for troubleshooting, but trace IDs must not be reversible to a subject identifier. We prefer either customer-provided salted hashing or short-lived mapping keys that expire. Can Redwood support customer-managed secrets for that mapping?
3) Retention: 90 days searchable is our baseline. Beyond 90 days we can accept encrypted cold archives for compliance, but access must require an audit request. Can you confirm Redwood will log purge operations (who requested, when) and provide an immutable audit trail?

Also, the example log shows full headers including Authorization: Bearer tokens. We cannot accept any persisted Authorization header values. Will Redwood strip/nonce/replace header values in all persisted logs by default?

If you can confirm the above points that will help our legal and infosec teams sign off. Friday 10am PT works for a quick call — please send an invite.

Thanks,

Hi all,

Quick technical notes to address Sarah's questions before the call:

- Field-level redaction: Redwood supports configurable ingestion rules that run before data is written. Rules can be regex-based (SSN, card numbers), NLP PII detectors, or explicit allowlists/denylists. Redaction is pluggable: you can choose "mask" (replace with ****), "drop" (remove the field entirely), or "hash" (salted SHA256 with customer-provided salt).

- Request vs response: rules run symmetrically for both request and response payloads. You can define separate rule sets if you need different behavior for incoming vs outgoing.

- Headers: header redaction is configurable by header name. Out-of-the-box we strip Authorization, Cookie, and Set-Cookie before anything is persisted. For additional headers you can provide a list and we will either remove values or replace with a static token (e.g., <REDACTED-HEADER>).

- Trace IDs: we recommend pseudonymizing trace IDs with a customer-managed HMAC salt; the runtime stores only the HMAC(trace_id) and never the raw trace_id when that option is enabled. That preserves correlatability across services without reversible identifiers. We can also support short-lived mappings for debugging that auto-expire and are logged as privileged operations.

- Retention & purge auditing: all purge operations generate an immutable audit event (user, timestamp, scope, prior-retention-window). Events are written to an append-only audit store and can be exported to your SIEM. We can include a 90-day searchable retention SLA in the contract; cold archive beyond that will be encrypted and access-controlled.

- Implementation notes: redaction is done in the ingest path (before KV caching and long-term logging). Sampling and partial retention are options if you want to persist non-PII telemetry at higher granularity while redacting sensitive fields.

I'll demo a sample redaction rule set during the sync. In the meantime, I attached a quick snippet of a config pattern (JSON) in the Drive link Marissa shared.
